added.title: Senior Manager, Digital Engineering
added.description:
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.

OUR MISSION

True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.

OUR VALUES

Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.

BENEFITS & PERKS*

Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options
Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave
Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees
And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays
Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.
Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles

YOUR MISSION

True Anomaly designs, sources, and manufactures spacecraft across a landscape of engineering and business systems — PLM, requirements/ALM, MBSE, and ERP — that today do not share a connected flow of product data. As Senior Manager of Digital Engineering, you will own the digital thread that changes this: the authoritative, traceable flow of product data across the entire lifecycle, and the internal platform and in-house software that make it real. Delivering this digital thread is a contractual requirement, so the mandate is concrete and the timeline is externally driven. This is a founding, hands-on leadership role — early on you will build the platform yourself and set its architecture and engineering patterns in code, while you hire and grow the software engineering team behind it, from early-career engineers to staff level, expanding as the mandate grows. As the team matures your hands-on share deliberately gives way to multiplying through others, but you stay close enough to the architecture to lead your engineers on the merits. The platform you build will give engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing one authoritative source of product data instead of manual exports and disconnected tools, with the auditability and traceability an ITAR/CUI environment demands. Integrations connect today's tools, which remain owned and administered by the teams that run them; over time, your team will build in-house systems of record wherever owning the software serves the company better than buying it.

This is a role for a builder who leads — an engineer who never stopped shipping and is energized by developing people and standing up a high-performing function from the ground up. It is not a fit for a pure people-manager who is years out of the code, nor for a senior IC who does not genuinely want to build and grow a team.

Responsibilities

Team Leadership & Development

Hire, coach, mentor, and grow a team of software engineers, from early-career to staff level.
Set clear goals, provide regular feedback, and support career development and growth planning for direct reports.
Foster a collaborative, high-ownership culture that thrives under fast-paced, high-stakes conditions.
Manage on-call and support rotations so the team can keep its software reliable in production.

Hands-On Technical Contribution

Build early: personally write production code for the platform's core services, integrations, and first applications while the team is small, establishing the architecture and patterns others will extend.
Stay hands-on as the team grows — through design and code review, prototyping hard problems, and pairing — enough to make sound technical calls and keep the trust of senior engineers.
Deliberately hand off and multiply: shift work to the team as you hire, avoiding becoming the bottleneck or single point of failure on any critical path.
Set and uphold the engineering bar for code quality, testing, and technical documentation by example.

Strategy & Program Ownership

added.title: Chief Architect, Product Engineering
added.description:
Aderant is a global industry leading software company providing comprehensive business management solutions for law firms and other professional services organizations with a mission to help them run a better business. We are motivated by a collective desire to drive the legal industry to the forefront of innovation. With over 2,500 clients around the world, including 95 of the top AmLaw 100 firms, we are changing the outside perception of the legal sphere; where there was once resistance to modernization, we are creating a culture that embraces new ideas and technology.

At Aderant, the “A” is more than just a letter. It is a representation of how we fulfill our foundational purpose, serving our clients. It embodies our core values and reminds us that to achieve success, every day must start with the “A”. We bring the “A” to life by fostering a culture of innovation, collaboration, and personal growth. We encourage our diverse teams to bring their whole selves to work – ideas, experience, and passion – to drive our mission forward.

Our people are our strength.

The Chief Architect owns the technical architecture vision and execution across Aderant's product portfolio, modernizing the ongoing evolution of our overarching application and platform architecture into a scalable, cloud-native SaaS environment with AI, data, and security at its core. This role is the company's trusted architecture strategist, driver, and collaborator to Product Management, App Engineering, Platform Engineering, and Cloud Operations and is equally comfortable working hands-on through challenging technical problems and hands-off, advising and governing at the portfolio architecture level. The Chief Architect can lead either through direct management of a shared architecture team or through a dotted-line model with embedded architects, and is comfortable representing and influencing architecture decisions with both C-level and senior technical law firm team members.

Core Focus Areas

SaaS: Move the platform from legacy and on-prem models to true multi-tenant, cloud-native SaaS.
App Architecture: Set standards for services, APIs, and infrastructure that scale and are secure by design.
AI: Design how AI and agentic capabilities integrate safely across products.
Data: Own technical data architecture across the portfolio, including modeling, governance, and access models.
Cloud: Lead multi-cloud infrastructure strategy with deep domain expertise in AWS and Azure.
Network: End-to-end network standards, from physical through application layers, balancing scalability and security.
Infrastructure: Set standards for infrastructure-as-code, observability, and disaster recovery.
Security: Secure-by-design principles embedded across architecture, in partnership with InfoSec and GRC.

What You'll Do

Set Aderant's technical architecture strategy across SaaS, cloud, AI, data, network, infrastructure, and security.
Translate strategy into standards, guardrails, and reference patterns that Product Management, App Engineering, Platform Engineering, and Cloud Operations build against.
Bring technical judgment into Product Management's roadmap conversations, informing trade-offs without owning the roadmap.
Represent the architecture vision to clients, from CIO/CTO-level briefings to technical deep dives.
Get hands-on with design reviews, prototypes, and challenging technical problems when needed.
Set standards for how App Engineering and Platform Engineering extend the core platform and AI backbone.
Lead adoption of AI and agentic patterns into product architecture, working directly with engineering teams on integration.
Partner with Cloud Operations on infrastructure resilience, cost efficiency, and operational standards.
Collaborate with Platform teams on cross-portfolio governance, data access, integration, and scalability decisions.
Partner with InfoSec and GRC to define and enforce security controls and compliance requirements.
Run recurring architecture and security review processes across product teams, surfacing risk early.
Mentor senior engineers and resolve cross-product architecture conflicts.

Experience

12+ years in software architecture, including 5+ years as an enterprise or chief architect.
Experience architecting multi-tenant SaaS platforms across multiple cloud providers.
Track record leading a legacy-to-cloud or on-prem-to-SaaS transition at scale.
Hands-on experience architecting AI and ML-integrated products.
Strong background in data architecture, governance, and strategy.
Solid grounding in network and infrastructure architecture, including zero-trust and IaC.
Deep knowledge of application security, with experience partnering directly with InfoSec and GRC.
Track record advising both product and engineering leadership on technical strategy and outcomes that support technical and business outcomes.
Comfortable engaging clients at both the C-level and technical level.
Experience leading architecture through both direct management and dotted-line influence.
Experience with AI tools and processes that benefit the technical and business outcomes of the product, engineering and client outcomes.
Legal tech or vertical SaaS background.
Experience with M&A-driven product consolidation.
Familiarity with compliance frameworks such as SOC 2 and ISO 27001.
Technical stakeholder management across Product, App Engineering, Platform Engineering, and Cloud Operations.

added.description:
Description of Position
The Director, IT Infrastructure Services, under the general direction of the Chief Information Officer (CIO), provides strategic, architectural, and operational leadership for Yavapai College's enterprise IT infrastructure across all district campuses and centers. This position is responsible for ensuring the reliability, security, scalability, and lifecycle integrity of the college's foundational technology services, which include campus and wide-area networking, server and virtualization platforms, data storage and backup, cloud services, database systems, physical security and access control, and voice/telephony communications.

The Director leads a team of systems/database administrators, network administrators, and physical security specialists. This position also serves as a senior member of the ITS leadership team, contributing to the district's technology plan, technology roadmap, and digital transformation initiatives.

This position partners closely with the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) and other ITS directors to ensure that infrastructure services are secure, compliant, and aligned with Yavapai College's institutional mission.

Key Responsibilities:
Strategic & Architectural Leadership

Collaborates with the CIO and ITS leadership team to develop, communicate, and execute the district's multi-year IT infrastructure strategy, ensuring alignment with the YC strategic plan and institutional priorities.
Establishes and governs enterprise reference architectures covering campus and wide-area networking, server and virtualization platforms, storage, data backup and recovery, unified communications, wireless, and data center systems.
Develops and maintains a cloud infrastructure strategy — covering public, private, and hybrid cloud platforms (e.g., Microsoft Azure, Microsoft 365) to ensure scalability, cost-effectiveness, and alignment with district modernization goals.
Contributes to the development and annual refinement of the YC Technology Plan and participates in IT governance committees (e.g., Technology Advisory Committee, Change Advisory Board).
Researches emerging infrastructure technologies and provides recommendations to the CIO on applicability and adoption.
Infrastructure Operations & Service Management

Oversee the design, operation, and lifecycle management of all district enterprise IT infrastructure services.
Ensures high availability, reliability, performance, and scalability of all infrastructure services through robust monitoring, capacity planning, lifecycle management, and vendor support agreements.
Establishes and matures IT service management (ITSM) practices aligned with ITIL frameworks, including incident management, problem management, change management, configuration management, and release management processes.
Monitors infrastructure performance metrics, incident trends, outage reports, and service delivery outcomes.
Disaster Recovery & Business Continuity

Leads disaster recovery (DR) and business continuity planning (BCP) for all infrastructure services, including development, documentation, regular testing, and alignment with college-wide continuity plans.
Leads major incident response for infrastructure outages, ensuring timely escalation, stakeholder communication, root-cause analysis, and implementation of corrective actions.
Security, Compliance & Risk Management

Partners closely with the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) to ensure infrastructure architecture, configurations, and operational practices align with the college's information security policies, standards, and applicable regulations.
Team Leadership & Professional Development

Provides direct supervision, performance management, and professional development for the Infrastructure Team.
Develop and implement succession planning and staff development pathways to build team depth and ensure operational continuity across all infrastructure domains.
Ensures infrastructure teams operate with a strong customer-service mindset, fostering collaborative relationships with other ITS teams, college departments, and all stakeholders.
Budget, Procurement & Vendor Management

Determines fiscal requirements, prepares annual and multi-year budget projections for the infrastructure domain, and monitors, verifies, and reconciles expenditures against budgeted funds.
Builds and manages strategic relationships with technology vendors, contractors, and consortium partners; leads contract negotiations for infrastructure-related hardware maintenance, software licensing, and service agreements.

Minimum Expectations & Requirements
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Information Systems, or a closely related field — OR an equivalent combination of education and professional experience sufficient to perform the essential duties of this position.

Experience:
Minimum of 8 years of progressive experience in enterprise IT infrastructure, with at least 3 years in IT management or supervisory role overseeing teams of technical professionals.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

Demonstrated knowledge of a wide range of infrastructure technologies and cloud services.
Demonstrated ability to develop and communicate IT infrastructure strategy, architecture, and roadmaps to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Working knowledge of IT service management (ITSM) frameworks, including incident, change, and problem management.
Proven ability to manage departmental budgets, vendor relationships, and multi-year capital planning for technology infrastructure.
Demonstrated commitment to customer service, team development, and cross-departmental collaboration.
Regular, reliable attendance and the ability to respond to after-hours infrastructure incidents when required.

Preferred Skills & Abilities
Education:
Master's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a closely related field.

Experience:
Higher education administrative experience, preferably in a community college environment.

Knowledge/Skills/Abilities:

Experience with Microsoft Enterprise Platforms (Azure, Entra, 365) and hybrid cloud architecture.
Relevant industry certifications such as: CCNA, CCNP, or CCIE (Cisco); Azure Solutions Architect; AWS Solutions Architect; CISSP; PMP; or equivalent.

added.title: Interim Chief Technology Officer
added.description:
Department Overview

The mission of the Information Technology Group (ITG) is to develop, implement and maintain technology-based services and solutions to enable OHSU to effectively manage information to accomplish its missions.

Reporting directly to the Senior Vice President and OHSU Chief Information Officer, the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a member of the ITG executive leadership team and sets the vision, strategy, and direction for OHSU's core technology infrastructure and architecture. The CTO has broad oversight of technology and infrastructure operations, projects and planning, and holds ultimate responsibility for the technology services components of OHSU's strategic and tactical initiatives. The CTO also positions the organization to adopt emerging technologies in ways that advance OHSU's clinical, research and academic missions.

The most critical function of the role is ensuring the ongoing, 24x7 operation of OHSU systems and networks. A stable, secure and resilient technology environment is vital to business continuity for the university.

The CTO leads the Technology Infrastructure, Design and Engineering (TIDE) Division, which delivers enterprise-wide core technology support including networks, compute and storage, telecommunications support, data centers, design and construction, collaboration and core applications and business continuity.

Function/Duties of Position

Technology Management

The strategic role of the Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is to establish direction and technology vision, to develop and pursue technical standards, to set general direction around core technology architecture and to evaluate and guide the adoption of emerging technologies. The operational role is to create and maintain the structure necessary to ensure business continuity through a stable technology infrastructure.

These Roles Translate To The Following Major Responsibilities

Responsible for defining a robust, scalable, extensible technology architecture that is fully integrated with the wider enterprise architecture and aligned with industry best practices.
Responsible for defining engineering and technical standards, processes and procedures for core technology, and ensuring consistent adoption across the division.
Directs the delivery and ongoing reliability of core technology services, systems and networks. Includes oversight of operational procedures and disaster planning. Ensures infrastructure is designed and maintained in accordance with security standards established by the Chief Information Security Officer and broader enterprise architecture strategy.
Responsible for establishing IT capacity planning to ensure technology infrastructure meets OHSU’s current and future needs. Proactively identifies technical infrastructure risks, emerging requirements and systems issues, and develops solutions.
Establishes and oversees performance metrics and measurements for division to inform tactical and long-range decision making.
Manage departmental operating and capital budgets and partner with Vendor Management to oversee strategic technology vendor relationships and contracts.

Division Leadership

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) provides supervision and mentoring to Directors and frontline managers in the division. These directors and managers have day-to-day, functional responsibility for their areas and their perspectives are best focused on their individual specializations. The CTO’s role is to ensure that the collective group works in a unified, collaborative, cohesive direction.

ITG Executive Management

The Chief Technology Officer (CTO) is a member of the ITG executive management team, which collectively strives toward the common goals, strategies and vision of ITG and OHSU. Works with executive management to determine and execute the strategic goals and initiatives in support of the broader organization.

As part of the executive team, the CTO will gain a broad view of OHSU’s IT strategies and operations, which they must translate to efforts, direction and oversight within the division.

The CTO represents ITG executive management on committees and other groups.

Required Qualifications

Education and Experience

Master’s degree in information technology or related field; OR
Bachelor’ s degree in information technology or related field and significant experience in Information Technology.
Minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible management positions in information technology.
Three years of experience in technology management at senior management level, including budgeting and financial reporting.
Experience evaluating business requirements, technology options, operating models, costs, risks, and governance considerations. Significant organizational and management skills, specifically within a large organization.
Experience developing and implementing IT strategies.
IT project/program management experience to successfully manage small- and large-scale applications projects.
Experience in a complex technology environment.

Skills And Abilities

Broad range of knowledge of IT systems, networks, telecommunications.
Effective leadership of highly skilled management and technical personnel in overseeing the development and implementation of technology strategy and planning.
Superior oral, written and communication skills.
Ability to operate in a highly stressful environment, demonstrating good judgment and creative/original thinking to address the demands of the business.
Ability to influence, motivate and provide clear direction.
Ability to use tact and diplomacy to maintain effective working relationships.
Skilled in overseeing multiple projects with budget responsibilities.
Demonstrated skill in managing operational and capital budgets.
Must have knowledge of ITIL service management concepts.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience managing in a union environment.
Experience in an academic health system, healthcare, higher education, or similarly complex regulated environment.
Expert knowledge in information technology (systems, telecommunications, networks).
Knowledge of healthcare, research and academic environments and applications.
Knowledge of quality management and performance improvement techniques.

Additional Details

Location: This position is eligible for hybrid-remote work, the work location will primarily be remote with with occasional meetings and events onsite at various OHSU locations.

Benefits

Healthcare for full-time employees covered 100% and 88% for dependents.
$50K of term life insurance provided at no cost to the employee.
Two separate above market pension plans to choose from.
Paid time off - 208 hours per year, prorated for part-time.
Extended illness bank - 64 hours per year, prorated for part-time.
9 paid holidays per year.
Substantial Tri-Met and C-Tran discounts.
Employee Assistance Program.
Childcare service discounts.
Tuition reimbursement.
Employee discounts to local and major businesses.

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center.

In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington.

All are welcome.

OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply.

added.description:
Position

Cincinnati Country Day School (CCDS) seeks a visionary, collaborative, and strategic technology leader to serve as its director of technology. Reporting to the head of school and serving as a member of the school's leadership team, the director of technology provides leadership, planning, management, and oversight for all aspects of the school's technology program, infrastructure, cybersecurity, instructional technology initiatives, and technology support services. The director of technology will develop and execute a comprehensive technology strategy that advances the school's mission, enhances teaching and learning, supports operational excellence, safeguards institutional data, and ensures the reliability and scalability of the school's technology ecosystem. The ideal candidate combines strong technical expertise with exceptional leadership, communication, project management, and strategic planning skills. This is a 12-month, full-time administrative position.

Responsibilities

The director of technology will:
Develop and implement a multi-year technology vision and strategic roadmap aligned with school priorities.
Serve as the primary advisor to school leadership regarding technology strategy, innovation, cybersecurity, infrastructure, and digital transformation.
Lead, mentor, and evaluate technology personnel and external technology service providers.
Build and manage technology operating and capital budgets.
Oversee technology procurement, vendor relationships, contract negotiations, and software licensing.
Establish and monitor technology governance, policies, standards, and best practices.
Lead technology-related risk management, business continuity, disaster recovery, and cybersecurity initiatives.
Collaborate with academic and administrative leaders to identify technology solutions that improve teaching, learning, communication, and operational efficiency.
Stay informed regarding emerging technologies, independent school technology trends, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity developments, and educational innovation.

Infrastructure and Systems Management

Provide strategic oversight and operational leadership for the school's technology environment, including:
Microsoft enterprise infrastructure supporting approximately 1,000 faculty, staff, and student devices.
Microsoft 365 services, including Entra ID, Intune, Teams, Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, and School Data Sync.
Active directory and hybrid identity management environments.
Windows Server, Azure Stack HCI, Hyper-V, SQL Server, and related enterprise systems.
Microsoft Surface device lifecycle management, deployment strategy, and endpoint security.
Enterprise networking infrastructure, including Extreme Networks and Aruba switching environments.
Campus-wide wireless infrastructure utilizing Extreme Cloud IQ. Network services including DNS, DHCP, NPS, file services, and print services.
Fortinet security platforms and related network security controls. Enterprise PKI and certificate management.
AudioCodes telephony infrastructure and SIP services.
Coro cybersecurity platform and cybersecurity monitoring initiatives.
Veracross Student Information System and related integrations.
Lenel OnGuard access control systems.
Google Cloud DNS and other cloud-based infrastructure services.

Cybersecurity and Data Protection

The director of technology will:
Lead the development and execution of the school's cybersecurity strategy.
Establish security policies, procedures, and standards aligned with industry best practices.
Conduct regular risk assessments and vulnerability management reviews.
Oversee identity management, endpoint security, security awareness training, and incident response planning.
Ensure compliance with applicable privacy and data protection requirements.
Manage cybersecurity vendors, audits, and remediation efforts.
Coordinate business continuity and disaster recovery planning.

Technology Operations

Ensure high availability and reliability of critical technology systems
Establish service delivery standards and performance metrics
Oversee incident management, problem resolution, and technology support operations
Promote operational excellence through automation, documentation, and process improvement
Utilize PowerShell, scripting, and automation platforms to improve efficiency and scalability
Develop and maintain comprehensive technology documentation, architecture diagrams, inventories, and operational procedures

Instructional Technology Leadership

Partner with school leadership and faculty to advance innovative uses of technology in teaching and learning
Evaluate and recommend instructional technology tools and platforms
Support professional development initiatives related to educational technology
Facilitate responsible and effective use of emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence solutions

Qualifications & Personal Attributes

Required

Bachelor's degree in information technology, computer science, educational technology, information systems, or a related field
Minimum of 7-10 years of progressively responsible technology leadership experience
Demonstrated success managing enterprise technology environments
Strong expertise with Microsoft cloud and on-premises technologies
Experience leading cybersecurity, infrastructure, systems administration, and network operations
Strong financial management and budgeting experience
Excellent leadership, communication, collaboration, and project management skills
Ability to communicate highly technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences

Preferred

Master's degree in a related field
Technology leadership experience in an independent school, higher education, or nonprofit environment
Microsoft, cybersecurity, networking, or project management certifications
Experience with Veracross or other student information systems
Familiarity with AI governance and responsible artificial intelligence implementation

Personal Characteristics

The successful candidate will demonstrate:
Strategic and innovative thinking.
Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills.
Sound judgment and decision-making abilities. A service-oriented leadership style.
A commitment to continuous improvement.
The ability to lead through change and foster collaboration across all constituencies.

To Apply

Interested and qualified candidates are invited to submit the following materials as separate PDF documents to Ashley Coates, assistant to the head of school, at coatesa@countryday.net.
A cover letter expressing their interest in this particular position.
A current résumé.
A list of three professional references with name, relationship, phone number, and email address of each (references will not be contacted without the candidate’s permission).

To learn more about Country Day, visit https://www.countryday.net/.

added.description:
Job Type

Full-time

Description

The Opportunity

Prime Residential is looking for a Vice President of Information Technology to own our entire technology environment and lead the next phase of how we use data and AI to run the business.

Prime owns and operates approximately 21,000 apartments across California, Washington, Oregon, and Nevada. Reporting to the Chief Financial Officer, the VP of IT leads Prime's IT organization, owns the technology vendor stack and budget, and serves on the Leadership Team as the executive accountable for one of the company's core objectives: leverage technology to efficiently manage and operate.

This is a broad seat. You will own the network and endpoints, cybersecurity, business applications, the property management platform, IT project management, and end-user support. You will also own the two areas where Prime is moving fastest: a trusted data architecture with reporting the business actually uses, and a real strategy for putting AI to work.

We are looking for an operator who modernizes. Someone who can keep 56 communities running while building what comes next, and who is comfortable being measured on both.

What You Will Do

Own and evolve a cloud-first enterprise technology strategy, architecture, and governance model, translating company objectives into a sequenced roadmap.
Build, coach, and retain the IT team, with a genuine focus on up-leveling individual skills and careers and creating bench depth so no system and no person is a single point of failure.
Own technology financial planning and the IT budget, including forecasting, prioritization, licensing optimization, and accounting for each dollar in terms of what it delivers.
Own IT project management end to end: demand intake, prioritization, governance, delivery performance, risk, budget, and benefits realization.
Own the Fabric data environment and the reporting layers built on it, with one source of truth, governed definitions, documented logic, and dashboards that are maintainable by more than one person.
Work aggressively to incorporate AI, including agentic AI, to improve the productivity of corporate and onsite teams; stand up and chair a cross-functional AI governance committee and publish a living AI use policy.
Provide executive oversight for the Microsoft cloud ecosystem, corporate infrastructure, and Prime's critical SaaS and line-of-business platforms.
Own the property management platform and surrounding PropTech stack, including leasing, work orders, resident communication, maintenance, screening and fraud controls, smart home equipment, access controls, and the integrations connecting them.
Run vendor selection, contract negotiation, and performance management, and rationalize the application portfolio by consolidating or retiring what no longer earns its cost.
Lead technology workstreams for acquisitions, integrations, platform migrations, and property takeovers, each with a reliable timeline and communication plan.
Own cybersecurity, identity, compliance, and privacy, along with business continuity and disaster recovery.

The Hiring Process

Submit your application through this posting
45-minute introductory call with Prime's VP of Organizational Development
1-hour virtual interview with the Chief Financial Officer
Panel interviews with technology, operations, and business leaders
Final in-person interview at Prime's San Francisco headquarters
Reference Checks
Offer extended
Background Check

Location and Travel

Based in Prime's San Francisco headquarters. Travel up to approximately 15% of the time, including visits to properties and regional offices, business meetings, training, and vendor or conference attendance.

Compensation

Prime Residential is an equal opportunity employer committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Requirements

10+ years in technology roles, including experience running IT for a multi-site field operation under a finance-driven corporate headquarters; Multifamily is ideal; hospitality, senior living, and other distributed operating businesses with an owned or managed asset base will be considered.
Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Master's a plus.
7+ years leading a team of five or more with full ownership of infrastructure, applications, and security, and a track record of developing people rather than only managing their output.
Direct experience owning a mid-sized or larger enterprise platform end to end: selection or migration, integration, adoption, ongoing operations, upgrade planning, and change management.
A track record of scaling IT systems, processes, and tools as an organization grew, including integrating acquired properties or portfolios onto a common platform.
Hands-on experience establishing technology policy, governance, and standards where none existed. AI governance built from the ground up is the strongest evidence; data governance, security governance, or a privacy program will also be considered.
Demonstrated experience putting data and AI to work in an operating business: building or maturing a data platform, delivering analytics that non-technical users adopted and kept using, and deploying AI tooling with appropriate guardrails.
Experience with Microsoft 365 and Azure, including identity, SSO administration, and Fabric, with experience migrating and operating cloud workloads and optimizing cloud spend.
Vendor and budget management experience at meaningful scale, including contract negotiation and portfolio rationalization.

Salary range of $253,000 to $282,000 + bonus

added.description:
EnableComp provides Specialty Revenue Cycle Management solutions for healthcare organizations, leveraging over 24 years of industry-leading expertise and its unified E360 RCM ™ intelligent automation platform to improve financial sustainability for hospitals, health systems, and ambulatory surgery centers (ASCs) nationwide. Powered by proprietary algorithms, iterative intelligence from 10M+ processed claims, and expert human-in-the-loop integration, EnableComp provides solutions across the revenue lifecycle for Veterans Administration, Workers’ Compensation, Motor Vehicle Accidents, and Out-of-State Medicaid claims as well as denials for all payer classes. By partnering with clients to supercharge the reimbursement process, EnableComp removes the burden of payment from patients and provider organizations while enabling accelerated cash, higher and more accurate yield, clean AR management, reduced denials, and data-rich performance management. EnableComp is a multi-year recipient the Top Workplaces award and was recognized as Black Book's #1 Specialty Revenue Cycle Management Solution provider in 2024 and is among the top one percent of companies to make the Inc. 5000 list of the fastest-growing private companies in the United States for the last eleven years. 

POSITION SUMMARY

The Vice President, Revenue Cycle Technology Operations leads the enterprise functions responsible for translating EnableComp's technology strategy into scalable, reliable, and measurable operational performance across revenue cycle service lines. Reporting to the Executive Vice President, Operations, this role owns the Technology Operations vision, investment portfolio, governance, and value-realization framework while setting the strategic direction, operating expectations, and performance framework for work delivered through EnableComp's global vendor partners. Serving as an executive bridge among Operations, Technology, Product, Data, Implementation, and external delivery partners, the VP aligns technology enablement, workflow design, capacity strategy, and partner performance with business growth and client commitments. The VP leads through internal leaders and designated vendor leadership, establishes decision rights and accountability, allocates resources, resolves cross-functional tradeoffs, and remains accountable for productivity, quality, cost, scalability, risk, employee experience, and client outcomes across the combined portfolio.

THE JOB RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE

Define and lead the enterprise vision, multi-year roadmap, and operating model for technology operations in alignment with EnableComp's growth strategy, client commitments, and Operations priorities.

Own the portfolio of Operations technology, automation, workflow-transformation, and global-operations initiatives, including business-case development, prioritization, sequencing, funding recommendations, and executive governance.

Establish decision rights, accountability, and ways of working across Operations, Technology, Product, Data, Implementation, Finance, Information Security, Compliance, and global vendor partners.

Translate business strategy and service-line needs into enterprise capability, capacity, and delivery requirements, ensuring technology and global-operations plans address the highest-value opportunities and risks.

Sponsor workflow redesign and standardization across onshore and global operations teams before and alongside technology deployment, ensuring processes are scalable, controlled, and consistently executed.

Set portfolio-level goals and KPIs for productivity, quality, cost-to-serve, cycle time, utilization, vendor performance, client outcomes, and return on investment; report results and recommendations to executive leadership.

Lead, develop, and hold accountable the Technology Operations leadership teams, including the Senior Directors, Revenue Cycle Technology Adoption..

Set strategic direction while delegating day-to-day technology adoption, global production, inventory coordination, vendor-team support, and performance-management execution to the respective Senior Directors.

Partner with Technology, Product, and Data leaders to align operational and global-delivery requirements with platform architecture, product roadmaps, integration capacity, data availability, and delivery constraints.

Maintain executive oversight of governance, operational continuity, regulatory and contractual controls, information security, data protection, third-party performance, and change risk; use performance data, partner feedback, and client insight to drive continuous improvement.

Sponsor pilots and phased rollouts, establish readiness and scale criteria, and make data-informed decisions to expand, revise, pause, or retire solutions.

Build a continuous-improvement culture that uses performance data, frontline feedback, client insight, and market developments to identify and deliver the next generation of operational capabilities.

Other duties as required.

REQUIREMENTS AND QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in business, healthcare administration, information systems, engineering, or a related field required; advanced degree (MBA or similar) preferred.

12+ years of progressive leadership experience in healthcare revenue cycle management, healthcare operations, technology-enabled services, or a related environment, including 5+ years leading at the senior director or vice president level.

Demonstrated success building and leading an enterprise technology-operations, digital-transformation, automation, or operational-excellence portfolio with measurable business outcomes.

Demonstrated success leading operational change in a services or operations heavy business, including at least one transformation carried through technology-led workflow redesign from pilot through multi-team rollout to a measured result, with task-level planning, dependency and gate management, and delivery at or under budget on a program with executive visibility.

Strong knowledge of healthcare revenue cycle operations, including complex claims, denials, reimbursement, revenue recovery, or adjacent workflows.

Experience governing cross-functional portfolios and partnering with Technology, Product, Data, Information Security, Finance, and Operations leaders in a matrixed organization.

Demonstrated financial and analytical acumen, including business-case development, investment prioritization, KPI design, benefits realization, and executive-level reporting.

Experience directing outsourced or global delivery partnerships, including vendor governance, service-level performance, capacity planning, commercial oversight, and risk management preferred.

Timely and regular attendance.

Equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

SPECIAL CONSIDERATIONS & PREREQUISITES

Practices and adheres to EnableComp's Core Values, Vision and Mission.

Enterprise mindset with the ability to balance growth, client, operational, financial, risk, and technology considerations when setting priorities.

Executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to translate complex operational and technical topics into clear decisions, tradeoffs, and actions.

Proven ability to lead through other leaders, build high-performing teams, and distinguish strategic accountability from delegated program execution.

Financially disciplined and data-driven, with the ability to connect technology investments to measurable operational and client value.

Skilled at influencing senior stakeholders, resolving competing priorities, and making timely decisions with incomplete information.

Ability to navigate ambiguity and lead effectively in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment.

What You Will Do

The Senior Manager, Technology Operations is a hands-on operational leader responsible for the stability, security, and scalability of Primrose School Franchising's technology environment. This role owns the day-to-day health of corporate and franchise-facing technology systems, leads the Change Advisory Board (CAB) process, manages the IT help desk, and serves as the primary point of accountability for infrastructure, cybersecurity, and vendor performance. Equally important is the ability to translate technology operations into business terms — communicating risk, cost, and capability to non-technical stakeholders across a 567-school franchise network. Infrastructure and Security

Lead capacity planning, lifecycle management, and refresh planning for hardware and software assets.
Oversee business continuity and disaster recovery planning, documentation, and annual testing.

Own the CAB process end-to-end: chair weekly meetings, maintain the change log, enforce change windows, and ensure proper risk assessment and rollback planning for all significant technology changes.
Drive continuous improvement of change management practices and educate stakeholders on the process.
Serve as the escalation point for emergency changes and conflict resolution between change owners.
Translate technology operations performance and risk into plain-language reporting for the executive leadership team.
Serve as the technology operations voice in cross-functional initiatives, including platform migrations, new school launches, and process improvement workstreams.

About Us

At Cloudflare, we are on a mission to help build a better Internet. Today the company runs one of the world’s largest networks that powers millions of websites and other Internet properties for customers ranging from individual bloggers to SMBs to Fortune 500 companies. Cloudflare protects and accelerates any Internet application online without adding hardware, installing software, or changing a line of code. Internet properties powered by Cloudflare all have web traffic routed through its intelligent global network, which gets smarter with every request. As a result, they see significant improvement in performance and a decrease in spam and other attacks. Cloudflare was named to Entrepreneur Magazine’s Top Company Cultures list and ranked among the World’s Most Innovative Companies by Fast Company.

At Cloudflare, we’re not looking for people who wait for a polished roadmap; we’re looking for the builders who see the cracks in the Internet that everyone else has simply learned to live with. We value candidates who have the instinct to spot a "normalized" problem and the AI-native curiosity to create a solution using the latest tools. Our culture is built on iteration, leveraging AI to ship faster today to make it better tomorrow, while ensuring that every improvement, no matter how small, is shared across the team to lift everyone up. If you’re the type of person who values curiosity over bureaucracy, and that AI is a partner in solving tough problems to keep the Internet moving forward, you’ll fit right in.

Location: Austin, TX | New York, NY | San Francisco, CA (metro areas)

About Cloudflare

At Cloudflare, our mission is bold yet simple: to help build a better Internet. Our global network handles trillions of requests each month, protecting and accelerating applications without added hardware, software, or code changes. The Developer GTM organization is a startup within Cloudflare, driving how we attract, inspire, and grow the next generation of builders. As the Senior Manager of Solutions Architecture for the AI & Developer Platform, you will lead a team of high-performing technical experts who help customers understand the business value and technical details of Cloudflare’s ecosystem. added.title: Senior Vice President of Engineering
added.description:
At Koalafi, we believe in a world where no one has to put an important purchase on hold. That's why we're making it easier for more people to pay for big purchases over time.

Retailers across the country rely on us to offer flexible lease-to-own financing to their non-prime consumers, while increasing sales and strengthening customer loyalty. Their 2M+ customers love us because we provide a flexible way for them to make payments and give them an opportunity to improve their credit. Our 200+ Koalafi teammates enjoy inspiring and challenging work that accelerates their careers.

Interested in learning more about how we're transforming the financing experience and joining our team?

The Opportunity

We're looking for a Senior Vice President of Engineering to lead Koalafi's entire engineering organization, including our Consumer and Merchant Experience, Core Engineering, and Application Experience groups, as well as our Data & AI Platform and Architecture functions.

Reporting to the Chief Product and Technology Officer, you will partner closely with the CPTO and Head of Product to set engineering direction, translate company priorities into execution, and build an organization that delivers meaningful business results. Your scope spans the platforms, applications, services, and data infrastructure that power our customer experiences, merchant relationships, and internal operations.

This is a company leadership role, not solely an engineering leadership role. You will help shape business decisions, influence across functions, and bring a clear perspective on how technology can support growth, improve efficiency, and strengthen the customer experience. You must be equally credible in a technical discussion with engineers and a strategic discussion with the executive team or the board—and move comfortably between those two modes.

We're also looking for an active AI practitioner who will help evolve how Koalafi works. You should be building and experimenting with AI tools yourself, with a thoughtful perspective on how to apply them across engineering and the broader business. The goal is not simply to increase adoption of tools or token usage, but to drive real, measurable business outcomes by embracing a willingness to fundamentally change how the business operates. You will lead this transformation through practical application, sound judgment, and measurable results.

What You'll Do

Set engineering direction and own execution

Partner with the CPTO, Head of Product, and cross-functional leaders to translate company objectives into a clear engineering strategy, investment priorities, and execution plans. Ensure teams understand the outcomes they are accountable for, make realistic commitments, and surface risks and tradeoffs early. Own the engineering response when delivery is at risk, aligning leaders on corrective action and following through.

Lead as a business executive

Build strong partnerships across Product, Risk, Operations, Finance, Sales, and other functions. Contribute to company decisions beyond engineering, connecting technical choices to growth, customer experience, operating efficiency, and risk. Communicate complex topics clearly and bring well-vetted recommendations – not simply issues or requests – to executive discussions.

Apply technical depth with sound leadership judgment

Earn the team's trust through technical expertise, thoughtful questions, and the ability to engage deeply in consequential architectural and engineering decisions. Recognize when an initiative, technical risk, or team challenge needs your direct involvement, and engage early enough to make a difference. Balance that involvement with clear delegation, strengthening your leaders' ownership rather than becoming a bottleneck or doing their jobs for them.

Build and develop a strong leadership team

Lead, coach, and hold accountable engineering leaders and managers across the organization. Set clear expectations for their technical judgment, business understanding, people leadership, and execution. Invest in succession planning, leadership development, and hiring, while addressing performance gaps directly. Continually evaluate team structure, responsibilities, and leadership capacity so the organization can operate effectively as priorities evolve.

Own architecture, data foundations, and pragmatic modernization

Guide the evolution of our applications, core services, and data platforms, balancing near-term delivery with long-term maintainability, reliability, and scale. Modernize the tech stack where it creates clear business value and be able to defend the ROI. Partner with Risk, Analytics, and Data Science to ensure our data engineering and AI foundations support reliable access, clear ownership, and effective use of data across the company.

Drive engineering excellence and responsible investment

Strengthen quality, test automation, delivery practices, observability, and operational readiness. Establish useful measures of delivery effectiveness, reliability, cost, and business impact, and use them to guide improvement. Own engineering budget and capacity planning in partnership with the CPTO and Finance, challenging staffing and technology proposals against business needs and credible alternatives. Partner closely with IT and Information Security to build and operate secure, resilient systems.

Lead AI adoption through hands-on practice

Maintain an active practice of building, prototyping, and experimenting with AI tools yourself. Use that experience to help teams improve how they design, build, test, deploy, and operate software—not just how they write code. Stay current with emerging capabilities, distinguish useful advances from hype, and turn promising experiments into repeatable practices with measurable improvements in speed, quality, or capacity, with the ultimate goal being to drive better business outcomes for the company.

Help the broader company work more effectively through AI

Partner with business leaders to identify where generative AI, automation, and better internal tools can improve workflows and outcomes. Help teams move from ideas and pilots to solutions people actually use. Ensure adoption is supported by appropriate data access, technical foundations, training, and safeguards, in partnership with Information Security, Risk, and Legal and Compliance.

About You

An experienced engineering executive. You bring 15+ years of progressive engineering experience, including substantial experience leading managers and senior engineering leaders across multiple teams. You have owned organization-wide strategy, delivery, talent, and investment decisions, not just an individual product or technical function.
Technically credible and comfortable going deep. You have strong architectural judgment across complex applications, distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and data platforms. You can challenge assumptions, assess tradeoffs, and help teams work through difficult technical decisions without needing to be the expert in every technology.
Business-minded and influential across functions. You understand how engineering decisions affect revenue, cost, customer experience, and risk. You can earn the confidence of executive peers, navigate competing priorities, and build alignment without relying on reporting lines or authority.
A leader with strong situational judgment. You know when to delegate, when to coach, when to challenge, and when to get directly involved. You maintain enough visibility to recognize emerging problems and take ownership before they become escalations, without micromanaging your team.
A committed developer of leaders. You have a track record of building inclusive, high-performing organizations and helping managers become stronger leaders. You set a high bar, provide candid feedback, address difficult people decisions, and create clear accountability.
An active AI practitioner. You can point to things you have personally built, workflows you have redesigned, or experiments you have run using AI tools. You have informed views on their capabilities and limitations, and experience helping others apply them effectively. Your interest extends beyond coding productivity to how AI can improve the way an entire company operates.
Pragmatic and accountable for outcomes. You can balance modernization with delivery, speed with reliability, and ambition with available capacity. You communicate clearly, make decisions with imperfect information, and follow through on commitments.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in fintech, payments, lending, or other regulated, transaction-intensive environments is a plus, as is experience with customer- and merchant-facing products, servicing platforms, and internal business systems such as Salesforce.
Familiarity with technologies in our environment—including Go, Node.js, React, AWS, Kubernetes, and native iOS and Android development—is helpful. We value strong engineering fundamentals and architectural judgment over expertise in any single stack.
Fluency in the modern AI stack and in how it is changing the way software is built. That includes frontier models, coding agents, and the harnesses, evaluations, and guardrails that make them reliable in production. You should understand how the developer workflow is shifting from writing code to designing and supervising agentic loops, where agents plan, build, test, and verify work against clear specifications. We standardize on Claude, but regularly evaluate new frontier models and tools, and knowing which advances actually matter, is a core part of the job.
Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Location:
Richmond, VA; Arlington, VA; or Remote (U.S.). Associates near one of our office locations may work in-office, hybrid, or remotely. Remote opportunities are available to candidates throughout the United States.

Salary Range:
$275,000-$325,000 per year (depending on experience and location)

Additional Compensation:
This position will be eligible to participate in company bonus plan.

The final salary offer will depend on factors including, but not limited to, experience, skills, and geographic location. The actual annualized salary amount offered to any candidate at the time of hire will be reflected solely in the candidate's offer letter.

Applications will be accepted until position is filled.

Why choose Koalafi:
A career at Koalafi means opportunities to tackle exciting challenges every single day. We take pride in a culture of innovation, trust, and ownership. You'll get outside your comfort zone, build meaningful relationships, and most of all, take charge of projects that ultimately help people get the things they need most.

We focus on what's most important

added.title: Senior Engineering Manager, Payments & Reconciliation
added.description:
At Commure, we're building the AI Operating System for healthcare, the foundation that defines how care is delivered, documented, and financed. Our platform spans the full care journey: Ambient AI and Dictation eliminating documentation burden at the point of care, intelligent Agents automating patient and revenue workflows, and autonomous RCM processing billions in claims, all on a single AI-native platform integrated with 60+ EHRs.

Healthcare carries a $1 trillion administrative burden and we're at the center of transforming it. Today, 500,000+ clinicians across 500+ healthcare organizations nationwide trust Commure to handle $25B+ in annual claims and support over 200 million patient interactions. Our latest $70M raise at a $7B valuation reflects the confidence the market has placed in this mission. We've also been named to the Fortune Future 50 list and the 2026 AI Breakthrough Awards for “Overall NLP Company of the Year.”

Our team works directly alongside clinicians, not through layers of process, which means the gap between what you build and its impact on patient care is immediate. We move fast, deploy daily, and take full ownership from early thinking to production. If you're energized by hard problems, high stakes, and a team that holds itself to a high bar, you'll find your people here.

The future of healthcare is being built right now. Come deliver this transformation.

About The Role

The Revenue Cycle Management team is hiring for a Senior Engineering Manager to join the team. We build software that helps medical practices get paid accurately. This role leads the engineering team that owns the money-in path: everything from when an insurer says how much they'll pay, to when that payment is on the books, verified against the bank, and the patient knows what they still owe.

You will manage a team of ~6 engineers across the full payments surface, reading insurer payment files, matching them to the right claims, recording money on visits, reconciling with bank deposits, calculating patient balances and collections, and partnering with the team that builds the financial reports clinics rely on.

A near-term priority is to hire 2 engineers to strengthen the team. You are the people leader and delivery owner: hiring, coaching, planning, and shipping outcomes, while staying close enough to the systems to set technical direction and unblock hard problems.

Together with teams that submit claims, handle denials, and build financial reporting, this group covers the path from "insurance paid us" to "the books are right, the patient knows what they owe, and leadership can trust the numbers."

What the Team Builds

Reading insurer payment files

Insurers send payment detail files (and paper explanations of benefits) through many networks and formats. The team ingests those files, turns them into structured payment records, and keeps each claim's status up to date as money comes in. This is the start of the pipeline — everything downstream depends on it being correct.

Matching payments to the right claims

Each payment line has to be linked back to the claim we originally submitted. Payers often send incomplete or inconsistent identifiers, so we use scoring across many signals (patient info, policy numbers, providers, amounts) and test changes on historical data before they affect real money.

Recording payments on the books

Once matched, payments are recorded on the correct visit using per-clinic rules — what to write off, what to shift to the patient, how contractual rates apply. Corrections use safe reverse-and-repost flows so history stays auditable. The books have to balance; "close enough" is not good enough.

Matching payments to the bank

For many customers, we verify that insurer checks actually landed in the clinic's bank account — using live bank connections, standard bank files, and scanned deposit slips. Until the deposit is verified, automatic recording of payments can be held. This includes the messy long tail of check numbers and payer names that don't match cleanly.

Patient balances and collections

After insurance pays, we calculate what the patient still owes and feed statements, the patient payment experience, credits, refunds, and collections. Balance logic has to keep up whenever posting or clinic rules change.

Financial reports clinics trust

The payment and ledger work this team owns feeds the reports and dashboards clinics use to run the business. You will partner closely with our financial reporting team so that billing, recorded payments, patient balances, and reports stay in agreement — catching drift early rather than after a customer notices it.

Scale: Large volumes of visits and payment lines, background jobs and scheduled pipelines, rule engines with hundreds of clinic-specific conditions, and zero tolerance for balances that don't add up.

What You'll Do

People & team leadership

Manage a team of ~6 engineers across payment file processing, matching, ledger recording, bank reconciliation, patient balances/collections, and integration with financial reporting.
Hire 2 engineers as an immediate priority; then continue to coach, retain, and grow the team through performance reviews, career development, and a healthy on-call culture.
Balance shipping new work vs. keeping money systems reliable — roadmap delivery without burning people out or risking incorrect balances.
Grow senior engineers who can deeply own areas (matching, posting, bank recon, patient billing) while the team still operates as one unit.

Technical & product leadership

Set direction for the full path: payment file to match to claim to record on books to adjust to verify in bank to patient balance to reports — where to invest for accuracy, reliability, and trust.
Align with neighboring teams (claims submission, denials, financial reporting, patient product, and operations) so handoffs are clear and problems are caught early.
Invest in visibility and operability: the ability to follow a payment from the insurer's file all the way to a patient balance and a report row — with dashboards and runbooks that work when something breaks overnight.
Guide careful changes to large databases and long-running jobs, with clear rollout and rollback plans.

Execution & planning

Own quarterly planning and goals; break large initiatives into small, shippable steps (better matching, higher bank match rates, faster/safer recording, fewer patient-balance surprises, clearer reporting handoffs).
Represent the team with product, operations, and leadership; communicate tradeoffs clearly.
Reduce repetitive support work: push clinic configuration toward self-service tools instead of one-off engineering changes.

Our Tech Stack

Backend: Python (FastAPI)

Database: PostgreSQL

Caching: Redis

Async processing: Background jobs, task queues, and schedulers for batch payment processing

Cloud: Major public cloud provider

Monitoring: Prometheus + Grafana

Frontend: React (and some Vue), plus reporting product surfaces

Collaboration: Notion, Linear

Required

What You Have

3+ years managing software engineers (hiring, performance, career growth), with experience leading a team of roughly 5-8+ engineers on backend-heavy systems
Track record shipping and operating financial, payments, billing, reconciliation, accounting, or collections systems in production — you understand why money systems can't be "eventually correct."
Strong enough technical judgment on large databases, background pipelines, and complex business rules to challenge designs, prioritize investment, and unblock escalations — without needing to write every line of code.
Experience partnering with operations or customer-facing teams when correctness and clear explanations matter.
Clear written and verbal communication; comfort owning incidents and summarizing them for stakeholders.

Strongly preferred

Healthcare billing, insurance payments, patient accounting, bank reconciliation, or practice-management background — or deep fintech / accounting-platform experience.
Experience with file-based integrations, matching/reconciliation problems, or high-volume batch pipelines.
Experience keeping operational systems and financial reports in agreement.
History of improving on-call quality, reducing time to recover from incidents, and testing high-risk automation before it ships.
Experience growing senior engineers across multiple problem areas on one team.

Strategic Architecture & Transformation
- Develop and maintain the enterprise architecture roadmap aligned with the organization's AI-driven digital transformation goals, business strategy, and long-term growth objectives.

The Company

An established, PE-backed B2B SaaS company operating in a regulated market is making AI a core part of its product strategy. The business has a substantial existing customer base, multiple production platforms, and a roadmap moving from relatively straightforward LLM applications toward more sophisticated agentic systems and AI infrastructure.

The Opportunity

This is a high-impact architecture role for someone who wants director-level technical influence without stepping away from the code. You will define how customer-facing AI is built across an established product portfolio while helping a broader engineering organization adopt stronger agentic, evaluation, context, and governance patterns.

The Role

You will own end-to-end architecture for the company’s customer-facing AI capabilities and lead a small senior AI team. This is explicitly a player-coach position: you will make major technical decisions, build reference implementations, work directly in the codebase, and enable product engineering teams to ship production AI safely at scale.

What You’ll Do

Own architecture across agentic workflows, compliance-focused AI, content generation, retrieval, memory, context, and other customer-facing AI capabilities.
Design agent architectures, orchestration patterns, MCP integrations, reusable context standards, and reference implementations for wider engineering teams.
Establish rigorous evaluation methodologies and quality standards for production AI features.
Lead build-versus-buy decisions covering models, infrastructure, hosting, evaluation, and supporting AI platforms.
Partner with product and platform engineering teams to prototype capabilities, move them into production, and transfer ownership without becoming a bottleneck.
Define technical approaches to data governance, tenant isolation, model hosting, privacy, cost management, and enterprise AI requirements.
Coach engineers through architecture reviews, workshops, demos, and hands-on collaboration while continuing to write production code.

What You’ll Bring

Software engineering experience, including senior technical ownership of a production AI product.
Proven experience designing and shipping agentic systems involving orchestration, tool use, multi-step workflows, memory, or context management.
Current hands-on knowledge of LLM application architecture, retrieval, evaluation, prompt/context engineering, and production AI systems.
Experience operating at SaaS scale and improving existing products and architectures rather than working exclusively on greenfield systems.
Ability to communicate complex architecture clearly to engineers, product teams, executives, and non-engineering stakeholders.
A collaborative player-coach approach: comfortable setting technical direction while building relationships, mentoring teams, and working through regulatory or organizational constraints.

What This Role Requires

Hands-on delivery of production agentic systems used by customers.
Current fluency across LLM application architecture and evaluation.
A genuine desire to remain hands-on in the code while operating at director level.

Why Join

Own one of the most strategically important technical areas in the business, with meaningful authority over AI architecture across multiple product teams.
Work on real production challenges across agents, retrieval, knowledge graphs, evaluation, privacy, governance, and AI infrastructure rather than isolated prototypes.
Keep building while operating at leadership level, with the opportunity to raise the technical standard for AI across a substantial engineering organization.

The 2028 Games mark the return of the Summer Games to the U.S. for the first time in 32 years and Los Angeles’ third time hosting an Olympic Games and first time welcoming the Paralympic Games. This presents the unique and exciting opportunity to celebrate our legacy with the Games and push the Olympic and Paralympic Movements forward, writing a new chapter of Games history in Los Angeles.

Putting on an Olympic and Paralympic Games is a team sport. To build a Games unlike any the world has seen before, we need the best team in place–a team full of diverse perspectives, experiences and expertise. We are guided by the following set of values and behaviors–optimism, integrity, excellence, inclusion, co-creation and boldness–and look forward to hearing about how your past experiences align with them.

Sr. Manager, Venue Infrastructure Delivery

The VNI (Venue Infrastructure) team plays a critical role in delivering competition and non-competition venues that are functional, innovative, and accessible for the Olympic and Paralympic Games. As part of the larger Sport & Games Delivery group, the VNI team ensures that all venues are designed and developed with the highest standards for functionality, sustainability, and inclusion.

As Sr. Manager of Venue Infrastructure Delivery, the role leads the end-to-end design, build, and delivery of a key Games-time venue. You will manage a team of 3–4 staff members alongside external partners and contractors. Initially, you will coordinate with internal teams, external partners, and consultants to finalize Olympic and Paralympic venue designs. Leadership

Ensure a robust, data-driven approach to venue design and delivery

Bachelor’s degree in Architecture, Engineering, Sports Management, Construction Management, Event Management, or related field or equivalent work experience strongly preferred

Familiarity with temporary infrastructure projects

Experience working with senior executives across multiple functional areas
Excellent leadership skills with track record of people development and revenue achievement
Extremely detail-oriented with excellent organizational skills
Strong communication, team building, and interpersonal skills
Well-developed problem-solving skills and ability to work independently to resolve issues
Fluent working with Office suite products including Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint
Self-starter with experience in defining tasks, seeking feedback, and evolving work where applicable
A collaborative mindset; someone who prioritizes the team and fosters a culture of high performance without ego
An innovative viewpoint, challenging the status quo and thinking ahead to future years of the Movement

The position is based in Los Angeles office with in-person presence required.
The LA28 office is an open-plan working environment; employees must be able to work efficiently in an open cubicle environment.
The majority of work will be conducted in an office setting, requiring extended periods of time sitting, standing, using computers, phones, and other office equipment, and attending in-person meetings.

Ability to work extended hours during critical build milestones and Games-time preparations
